clue.text: Split personality, perhaps

parts.note: reads as a psychiatric disorder, but Split is the Adriatic port city, so a person from there was once a citizen of that Balkan federation

explanation.surface: A psychiatrist hesitantly diagnoses a patient with a divided mind.
explanation.walkthrough: The capital S of Split is hidden at the start of the clue: Split is a city in Croatia, formerly part of Yugoslavia, so a 'personality' from Split might be described by this nationality.
explanation.definitionFit: A native of Split, the Croatian city, would have held this federal Balkan nationality before 1991.

clue.text: System of exercises for Indian clubs?

definitions.text: System of exercises for Indian clubs?

parts.words: System of exercises for Indian clubs?
parts.note: Indian clubs are gym equipment, but here the clubs are societies of Indian ascetics and the exercises are their meditative discipline

explanation.surface: A fitness regime built around swinging Indian clubs.
explanation.walkthrough: Indian clubs are bottle-shaped gym weights; read 'clubs' as groups of Indian holy men, whose discipline is meditation and postures.
explanation.definitionFit: The practice of the Hindu discipline of meditation and postures is a system of physical and mental exercise from India.

clue.text: Father of the power-station?

parts.note: a father is one who begets, and in a power station the machine that begets electricity is the dynamo

explanation.surface: Asking who first founded the power station.
explanation.walkthrough: To father is to beget or produce; the machine that produces electricity in a power station is named for producing.
explanation.definitionFit: A dynamo produces current, and a person who begets or originates something can be called by the same word.

clue.text: Cutting attack, in endless massacre, possibly

indicators.note: possibly signals that the remaining letters may be arranged in another order
the word massacre loses its final letter, so it has no end

explanation.surface: A vicious assault happening during a never-ending slaughter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endless' drops the last E of MASSACRE, leaving MASSACR, and 'possibly' rearranges it; 'in' is a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Biting mockery is a cutting verbal attack.

clue.text: Kind of tag left round end of lace

definitions.text: Kind of tag left round end of lace

parts.words: Kind of tag left round end of lace
parts.note: describes the small metal or plastic sheath fixed round the tip of a shoelace

explanation.surface: A tag someone has left wrapped around a shoelace tip.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue is a description: the little sheath crimped round a shoelace tip stops it fraying.
explanation.definitionFit: The small plastic or metal sheath at a shoelace tip is this kind of tag.

clue.text: Common trouble, getting vessel into well

indicators.note: the vessel is placed into the word for well, so one piece sits inside the other

parts.note: hale means healthy, in good health
SS is the abbreviation for steamship, a vessel

explanation.surface: Getting a boat down into a well causes everyday difficulties.
explanation.definitionFit: Ordinary bother or annoyance is what this informal word for trouble describes.

clue.text: Old Iago, the ensign

definitions.meaning: Iago in Shakespeare's Othello is called the ensign, an archaic word for which is also this word

explanation.surface: Shakespeare's villain, the standard-bearer, is getting on in years.
explanation.walkthrough: In Othello, Iago is repeatedly called Othello's 'ancient', an old word for an ensign or standard-bearer.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means aged or of long ago, and was an Elizabethan term for a standard-bearer, Iago's rank.

clue.text: Point, say, to a bright star

definitions.meaning: in botany a spike or pointed ear of grain goes by this Latin word
the brightest star in the constellation Virgo

explanation.surface: Someone points out a brilliant star in the night sky.
explanation.walkthrough: The Latin for an ear of corn, a spike, names the star held in Virgo's hand; 'say' marks a spike as an example of a point.
explanation.definitionFit: The Latin word for an ear of grain, a spike or point, also names the brightest star in Virgo.

clue.text: Circus-performer beating' the panel?

indicators.note: the panel takes a beating, its letters knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A big circus animal is thumping the panel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'beating' rearranges the eight letters of THE PANEL.
explanation.definitionFit: The big-eared pachyderm was a classic circus act, a performing animal in the ring.

clue.text: Redskin state in slavery, the main concern

indicators.note: the answer lies in the words slavery, the main, spanning them
the words slavery, the main concern the answer, holding it within them

explanation.surface: The main worry about a people kept in slavery.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Redskin' reads as a dated term for a people, but it means skin that is red; the answer spans 'slavERY THE MAin'.
explanation.definitionFit: This medical term names reddening of the skin from inflammation or dilated vessels.

clue.text: ECG erratic — panel ordered no, specific treatment

indicators.note: the letters of the three words are ordered afresh, put into a new sequence

explanation.surface: A medical panel orders no particular treatment after an irregular heart trace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'erratic' looks like the anagram signal for ECG, but it is fodder too: 'ordered' rearranges ECG, ERRATIC and PANEL, fifteen letters in all.
explanation.definitionFit: Family doctors practise medicine generally rather than in a specialism, so their work is non-specialist treatment.

clue.text: Jeeves, for example, would be watchful if old boy were in front

indicators.note: the abbreviation for old boy would stand in front of the answer to make the word for watchful, so it is taken away from that word

parts.note: observant means watchful, alert
OB is the abbreviation for old boy, a former pupil

explanation.surface: Wodehouse's valet would be more alert if an old schoolfellow led the way.
explanation.walkthrough: Jeeves is the valet in P G Wodehouse's comic novels; an old boy (OB) is a former pupil of a British school.
explanation.definitionFit: Jeeves is a valet, a domestic employee in a gentleman's household.

clue.text: Laundry-bay?

parts.note: laundry is a household's dirty clothes awaiting cleaning, and the bay is a large square inlet of the North Sea on England's east coast

explanation.surface: A space in the house set aside for doing the washing.
explanation.walkthrough: The bay is an inlet of the North Sea between Lincolnshire and Norfolk; the same three-plus-four words mean the laundry waiting to be cleaned.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means both a load of laundry and the large inlet on the English east coast.

clue.text: Running out of stock

parts.note: sounds like a shop with empty shelves, but stock here means livestock, cattle running in a mass panic

explanation.surface: A shop is selling out of its goods.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out of stock' suggests empty shelves; stock is livestock, and running is the headlong rush of a frightened herd.
explanation.definitionFit: A sudden panicked rush of a herd of cattle or horses is this kind of mass flight.

clue.text: With sixth sense get a position right for the trellis

parts.note: ESP, extrasensory perception, is the sixth sense
lie is a position, as in the lie of the land

explanation.surface: With intuition, find the right spot for the garden lattice.
explanation.walkthrough: The lie of a golf ball is its position.
explanation.definitionFit: A lattice framework on which fruit trees are trained flat is this kind of trellis.

clue.text: Plant Browning's snail lived on?

definitions.meaning: a prickly shrub, such as hawthorn
in Robert Browning's Pippa Passes the song runs 'The snail's on the ...', so this is where the poet put the snail

explanation.surface: A gardener wonders which plant the poet's snail made its home.
explanation.walkthrough: Pippa's song in Browning's verse drama Pippa Passes includes the line 'The snail's on the thorn; God's in his heaven'.
explanation.definitionFit: A hawthorn or other spiny shrub is this plant, and Browning's song places the snail on one.

clue.text: One-nil away, Liverpool's transferred too many people

indicators.note: the letters left are transferred into a new order
one nil, an O, goes away from the letters of Liverpool's

parts.note: the club's name with its possessive S counts as letters here
one nil, a single zero, is one letter O

explanation.surface: Liverpool, one-nil down away from home, sell off surplus players.
explanation.walkthrough: 'away' removes one O (a nil) from LIVERPOOLS, leaving LIVERPOLS, and 'transferred' rearranges it; the football surface hides it.
explanation.definitionFit: Surplus population moving out of a crowded city to new towns is this kind of excess.

clue.text: Factory dance-studio

parts.note: works is a factory, as in a steelworks
a hop is an informal dance

explanation.surface: A factory's dance studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dance-studio' looks like one compound, but the hyphen hides a break: HOP comes from 'dance' and 'studio' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A room where people make or create things, or where a group studies a craft, is a studio of sorts.

clue.text: Florentine gold lace

definitions.meaning: the Florentine iris gives a fragrant root used in perfumery, named after this word
an old word for lace made of gold or silver thread

explanation.surface: Lace with gold thread from Florence.
explanation.walkthrough: Orris root comes from the Florentine iris; separately, the same word once meant gold or silver lace.
explanation.definitionFit: The Florentine iris yields the perfumer's root of that name, and the word also named gold or silver braid.

clue.text: Mature in the ways of the common tiger

indicators.note: mature is placed in the ways, one piece sitting inside the other

parts.note: STS, streets, abbreviates ways or roads
ripe means mature

explanation.surface: Learning the habits of the everyday big cat as it matures.
explanation.walkthrough: St is the abbreviation for street, so STS stands for streets, i.e. ways. Stripes is a common pet name for a tiger.
explanation.definitionFit: A tiger is a striped cat, and this is a common pet name for one.

clue.text: One attending Her Majesty's royal court etc, we hear?

definitions.text: One attending Her Majesty's royal court etc, we hear?

parts.words: One attending Her Majesty's royal court etc, we hear?
parts.note: looks like a courtier at the palace, but Her Majesty's and the Royal Court are London theatres, where one hears a performance

explanation.surface: A courtier attending the Queen at her palace.
explanation.walkthrough: Her Majesty's and the Royal Court are London theatres; 'we hear' points to an audience listening to a performance.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who regularly attends theatres, such as these London ones, is a theatregoer.

clue.text: Familiar RAF officer who follows the band?

definitions.meaning: an informal nickname for a group captain in the Royal Air Force
an ardent fan who trails a pop band around

explanation.surface: An RAF officer who trails after a pop group.
explanation.walkthrough: The OCR dropped 'who'; RAF slang shortens group captain to this word.
explanation.definitionFit: RAF slang for a group captain and a fan who follows a rock band on tour share the word.

clue.text: Socialist party leaders present for the ball

indicators.note: the leaders of socialist and party are their first letters

parts.note: here means present, in attendance

explanation.surface: Left-wing party leaders attend the dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'ball' suggests a dance the leaders attend; it means a round body.
explanation.definitionFit: A ball is a round solid, a globe.

clue.text: Bird damaging' trees in Kuala Lumpur is still in the air

indicators.note: the rearranged trees go in between the letters of the city abbreviation

parts.note: KL is the usual abbreviation for Kuala Lumpur, capital of Malaysia

indicators.note: the word trees is damaged, its letters knocked into a new order

explanation.surface: A hovering bird of prey watches trees being wrecked in the Malaysian capital.
explanation.walkthrough: 'damaging' rearranges TREES to ESTRE, and 'in' puts that inside KL; the tail 'is still in the air' describes the bird's hovering.
explanation.definitionFit: This small falcon is a bird famous for hovering motionless while hunting.

clue.text: Switchgear?

parts.note: electrical switching equipment, but read as switch plus gear: to change and to move a gear lever

explanation.surface: Equipment for switching an electrical circuit.
explanation.walkthrough: Switchgear is electrical equipment; split it as switch and gear and the word means to change, as with a gear lever.
explanation.definitionFit: To switch or change something is this verb, and in American usage the gear lever is also called this.

clue.text: Where Derbyshire people take a shine to work

parts.note: gloss is a shine or lustre
op is short for opus, a work

explanation.surface: Residents of a Derbyshire town take a liking to their jobs.
explanation.walkthrough: Glossop is a market town in Derbyshire, a county in the English Midlands; 'take a shine to' looks like an idiom for liking, but the words split.
explanation.definitionFit: This market town in the High Peak is a place in Derbyshire where people live.

clue.text: Reading between the lines

parts.note: an idiom for inferring hidden meaning, but here a reading taken from a dial, and the distance between railway lines

explanation.surface: Inferring what someone really means.
explanation.walkthrough: The idiom misleads: an instrument gives a reading, and the distance between railway lines has the same name.
explanation.definitionFit: A measuring instrument gives a reading, and the spacing between railway tracks is called by the same word.

clue.text: Reprieve puts him free — one who could still get the chair

definitions.text: one who could still get the chair

indicators.note: the letters are set free and recombined into a new order

explanation.surface: A condemned man is reprieved, but might still face the electric chair.
explanation.walkthrough: 'the chair' suggests execution, but it is the throne: the next in line until a nearer heir is born could still succeed.
explanation.definitionFit: A presumed successor to the throne, displaceable by a nearer-born heir, may yet sit on the throne.

clue.text: Grass has to be treated with chemical

parts.note: pot is slang for cannabis, also called grass

indicators.note: the word has is treated, worked into a different order of its letters

explanation.surface: A lawn must be dressed with a chemical fertiliser.
explanation.walkthrough: 'to be treated' rearranges HAS to ASH, which follows POT.
explanation.definitionFit: Potassium carbonate and related potassium compounds go by this name, a chemical used in fertilisers.

clue.text: Early-warning system put out by Air Force?

definitions.text: Early-warning system put out by Air Force?

parts.words: Early-warning system put out by Air Force?
parts.note: suggests radar defences, but the early warning is the bugle call that wakes troops in the morning

explanation.surface: The air force installs a radar network to detect incoming attack.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Early-warning system' is a radar term, but here it means a call to wake service personnel early in the morning.
explanation.definitionFit: A bugle call sounded at dawn wakes soldiers or airmen, an early warning to rise.
